span: conviction could be sustained on the basis of last seen, motive and recovery of incriminating articles in pursuance of the information given by the accused if those five golden principles of the proof of a case based on circumstantial evidence are satisfied
why: Court states that, as unfailingly followed, a conviction can be sustained on circumstantial evidence when the five principles are met.

span: the prosecution has failed to adduce sufficient evidence to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubt
why: Appellants' counsel argues the circumstantial case is insufficient; a party submission, with the court's response in later paragraphs.

span: Whether the chain of circumstantial evidence is complete and consistent for arriving at the conclusion of guilt?
why: Frames the issues for decision; no position taken in the passage.

span: mere proof of receipt of money by the accused in the absence of proof of demand of illegal gratification is not sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused
why: Corruption case argument about proof of demand, not circumstantial evidence generally; a party submission.

span: There is no eye witness and the case rests only on circumstantial evidence.
why: Background statement of the type of evidence; the court's view is not in the passage.

span: Whether circumstantial evidence is sufficient to convict the accused
why: Headnote lists the issue and facts; the holding appears in the next passage.

span: several such evidences taken together may carry enough probative force to justify the conviction
why: Headnote holding: accumulated circumstantial evidence forming an unbroken chain can justify conviction.
